title.narrative: Addressing the emergency needs of IDPs mostly affected by natural disaster through provision of NFIs and plastic sheets in Beletweyne district.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 14px line-height: 115% color: black"gtDue to a greater than 90 per cent chance of El Nino continuation through the end of the year 2023 that will affect 1.2 million people in areas at high risk of flooding in Beletweyne district in Hiiraan region in Hirshabelle State.lt/spangtltem style="font-size: 14px"gtltspan style="line-height: 115% font-style: normal"gt lt/spangtlt/emgtltspan style="font-size: 14px line-height: 115% color: black"gtThis project is designed to provide early life-saving assistance to IDP communities projected to be most affected by El Nino riverine flooding in Beletweyne district – Hiiraan region who are in urgent need. Through the proposed initiative, HINNA will distribute standard Non-Food Items (NFIs) kits with 2 additional plastic sheets to 3781 households (approx. 22,686 persons) who will be selected from the most vulnerable groups including households living in deplorable shelter conditions, those who have lost household items and shelter during reverine floods, persons with disabilities, households with a large number of children between the ages of 6 months and 5 years, female-headed households, pregnant and lactating mothers, GBV survivors as referred by protection partners, and people from marginalized groups. As per the shelter cluster standards, each NFI kit will contain core items such as 1 Plastic Sheet, 3 Blankets, 2 Sleeping Mats, 1 Kitchen Set, 1 double Mosquito Net, 1 Solar lamp (torch) and 2 Jerry cans (10 litres) with built-in handle each and 2 additional plastic sheets for each HHs. Each household will receive both standard NFI kits and Plastic Sheets. At the onset of the project, 100 people from project target community will be mobilized about project information, scope, the beneficiaries’ selection process etc. Data collected to inform beneficiary selection will be segregated by gender and disability to ensure that no group is left out. Through distribution process, full beneficiary details will be captured including their contact telephone numbers and original thumbprints to facilitate future ME and impact evaluation processes. Utilizing its field expertise, HINNA will ensure safe distribution of NFIs through transparent selection of beneficiaries, promoting the active participation of beneficiaries in all project phases and equitable inclusion of the different fabrics of the target community. To mainstream protection and ensure that the unique needs of women, men, boys and girls are addressed during distribution processes, HINNA will adapt a number of strategies. These include establishing separate queuing lines for men and women, where necessary, and ensuring the presence of female team members at distribution sites to promote inclusion. As well, special arrangements will be made for the delivery of relief items to persons who have difficulty accessing the distribution point or carrying the kits, such as the disabled. All distribution activities will take place during daylight hours to allow beneficiaries sufficient time to travel home before nightfall or the distribution will take place in their IDP sites, but depending on their willing to do one of these aspects. During project implementation, women will be engaged in all project phases and decision-making processes as are aware of cultural norms. A Community Response and Feedback Mechanism (CRFM) will be established to ensure accountability to the affected population. Four (4) to six (6) weeks after the distribution, HINNA will conduct post distribution monitoring (PDM) using the harmonized PDM tool. The proposal is intended to lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtimplement through joint targeting the same location and same populations in close coordination with other humanitarian actorslt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px line-height: 115% color: black"gt lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtwho are implementing other sectors such as WASH, Protection, Food lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px line-height: 115% color: black"gtsecurity, Health, etc that will ensure a holistic and effective action for early lifesaving interventions to accelerate recovery for the target population affected by riverine floods.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
